slides.title: 02 WG Draft Updates (drafts not on agenda)
04 Applicability of IETF-Defined Service and Network Data Models for Network Slice Service Management

chat.author: Vishnu Beeram
chat.text: :grinning:

chat.author: Tony Li
chat.text: I'll settle for a room that's dry.

chat.author: Ran Atkinson
chat.text: Dry is nice.

chat.author: Reshad Rahman
chat.text: As NMOP co-chair: I didn't get the reference to NMOP

chat.author: Ran Atkinson
chat.text: It would be nice if the recharter does include RSVP security -- which (based on the slide) I think already is the plan.

chat.author: Adrian Farrel
chat.text: Perhaps broaden to "security for TE"?

chat.author: Vishnu Beeram
chat.text: @Adrian --Ack

chat.author: Ran Atkinson
chat.text: @Adrian: I am not sure what difference you see.

chat.author: Adrian Farrel
chat.text: RSVP is one protocol

chat.author: Adrian Farrel
chat.text: Well, RSVP-TE is our one protocol

chat.author: Ran Atkinson
chat.text: Which other protocols are you thinking about?

chat.author: Adrian Farrel
chat.text: Weeeell, I guess we should care about OSPF-TE and ISIS-TE. (Yeah, I know, LSR WG, but the needs for TE might be different.)

chat.author: Adrian Farrel
chat.text: Possibly no one cares about LMP any more

chat.author: Ran Atkinson
chat.text: Changes to OSPF or IS-IS belong in LSR, though cross WG reviw is always good.

chat.author: Adrian Farrel
chat.text: Suppose someone wanted to write a "Security Risks and Operational Guidance for TE Systems"

chat.author: Ran Atkinson
chat.text: I do not happen to have seen any LMP on the wire in recent years. It might still be used someplace, of course.

chat.author: Vishnu Beeram
chat.text: We have added some text related to RSVP-TE security in the proposed text; Keeping a broader TE scope in the charter seems appropriate

chat.author: Adrian Farrel
chat.text: Text such as, "Security for TE (especially for RSVP-TE)"

chat.author: Vishnu Beeram
chat.text: wfm

chat.author: Jie Dong
chat.text: Is the security of centralized-control based-TE also in scope?

chat.author: Vishnu Beeram
chat.text: The umbrella scope that Adrian proposed covers that as well..

chat.author: Adrian Farrel
chat.text: @jie Hence my suggested document

chat.author: Jie Dong
chat.text: OK, thanks for the confirmation

chat.author: Dhruv Dhody
chat.text: Is this still rfc8453?

chat.author: Adrian Farrel
chat.text: @dhruv I think so

chat.author: Adrian Farrel
chat.text: But question is whether MDSC-A acts as a CNC to MDSC B, or whether MDSCs can talk as peers

chat.author: Adrian Farrel
chat.text: I think this should be compared to peer PCEs and hierarchical PCE

chat.author: Dhruv Dhody
chat.text: To me ACTN is hierarchical by architecture and i am not able to envision the peer relationship

chat.author: Adrian Farrel
chat.text: Right. So we should clarify the use case (which I think is agreed) and then look to the different architectural solutions. And only then work on protocol

chat.author: Dhruv Dhody
chat.text: +1 Paolo

chat.author: Dhruv Dhody
chat.text:
RFC abstract says -- Abstraction of network resources is a technique that can be applied
   to a single network domain or across multiple domains to create a
   single virtualized network that is "under the control of a network
   operator" or the customer of the operator that actually owns the
   network resources.

chat.author: Adrian Farrel
chat.text: Right
